old.claim: Integrating the periodization over a fundamental cell, local finiteness gives a finite sum of integrals. Translating each cell by $Ln$ partitions the support of $y\mapsto\ell^{-d}K(y/\ell)$, so linearity and translation change of variables turn their sum into $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\ell^{-d}K(y/\ell)\,dy$. Apply [F2] to $g(s)=\ell s$ and $f(y)=\ell^{-d}K(y/\ell)$; the integral is $\int K(s)\,ds=1$.

proposed.claim: Choose the centered closed period cell $Q=[-L/2,L/2]^d$. For $r\in Q$ and $n\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}$, one coordinate of $r+Ln$ has absolute value at least $L/2>\ell$, so its kernel summand is zero. Thus on $Q$ the periodized kernel is $f(r)=\ell^{-d}K(r/\ell)$, whose support $\ell\operatorname{supp}K$ is compactly contained in $B_\ell(0)\subset\operatorname{int}Q$. Its period-cell integral is therefore its integral over $\mathbb R^d$. Step 1.2 gives compact-support Riemann integrability. Apply [F2] on the open domain $V=\mathbb R^d$ with $g(s)=\ell s$. This map is a global $C^1$ diffeomorphism with image $\mathbb R^d$, $|\det Dg|=\ell^d$, and hence $\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq g(V)$; zero extension outside $V$ is vacuous. The transformed integrand is $K(s)$, giving $\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}G_\ell=\int_{\mathbb R^d}K=1$.

old.claim: With an additional smooth periodic factor $q(x-r,t)$, the same finite-cell translation and periodicity give $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\ell^{-d}K(y/\ell)q(x-y,t)\,dy$. Applying [F2] to $g(s)=\ell s$ changes this to $\int_{\mathbb R^d}K(s)q(x-\ell s,t)\,ds$, proving the Euclidean representation.

proposed.claim: With the additional smooth periodic factor $q(x-r,t)$, the centered-cell argument in step 2.1 identifies the convolution with $\int_{\mathbb R^d}f_{x,t}(y)\,dy$, where $f_{x,t}(y)=\ell^{-d}K(y/\ell)q(x-y,t)$, componentwise. Each such integrand has support contained in the same compact set $\ell\operatorname{supp}K$ and is Riemann integrable by step 1.2. Apply [F2] with the same global dilation $g(s)=\ell s$ on $V=\mathbb R^d$; its image contains this support, its derivative is invertible, and zero extension outside $V$ is vacuous. The transformed integrand is $K(s)q(x-\ell s,t)$, proving the stated Euclidean representation.
